#4941. The 91 Best Movies of 2026 So Far (and 14 More We Can't Wait For)

With Christopher Nolan, star-studded epic romance, and major Marvel events, this list is a behemoth. And it also features a movie called Behomoth!.

AS A HUGE fan and follower of both movies and sports, the former has one major advantage: There's always something to look forward to. As a fan of the New York Jets, I don't always have that luxury. As a fan of watching films, though, not only is there always something worth my time on the big screen or streaming, but there's always several flicks down the line that will sound great or intriguing for one reason or another. Will they all turn out great? Of course not. But with sports and movies alike, excitement tends to be all about hope.

After a particularly strong 2025—movies like One Battle After Another and Sinners proved to be true standouts—how does 2026 pick up? With strength and energy, that's how. The year has been filled with all sorts of great movies, from horror (like 28 Years Later: The Bone Temple and Obsession) to epics (like The Odyssey), to some pretty great comedies (like Nirvanna the Band the Show the Movie and The Invite). It’s been a good year.

But we always like to look at not only what’s been good to date, but also what we can still be excited for—and that includes everything. We’re talking stuff on the calendar already, stuff we suspect could come out this year, and even stuff making noise in places like the Sundance Film Festival. Throughout the year, this list evolves from our most anticpated movies into our favorite movies, and always looks quite different in December than it did in January.

For now, we've got a lot we’ve loved, but still a lot to look forward to as well. Below, we've listed nearly 100 movies on our radar that we think you'll be really interested in seeing.

If you're interested in a killer chimpanzee B-movie slasher, then Primate is for you. The movie delivers what it promises. Ben the chimpanzee does some very terrible things on screen but it makes for quite an enjoyable experience.

28 Years Later: The Bone Temple is a direct sequel to last year's 28 Years Later. And while the great Danny Boyle doesn't return to direct, the movie is helmed by the more-than-capable Nia DaCosta and once again counts Alex Garland as its screenwriter. The real assets, though, are the movie's leads: Ralph Fiennes and Jack O'Connell are sensational, magnetic every minute they're on screen amidst all sorts of post-apocalyptic chaos. Bring on part three.

Here's a quick pitch for The Rip: Matt Damon and Ben Affleck. The longtime friends team up once again for The Rip, a cop thriller in the vein of movies you've probably seen several times before... but done particularly well. This twisty crime story involves a police team finding a ton of money in a stash house (the titular rip), and figuring out who may or may not be corrupt. In addition to our beloved duo, the cast is shockingly stacked: Steven Yeun, Kyle Chandler, Scott Adkins, and One Battle After AnotherAcademy Award nominee Teyana Taylor are all on board.

SAM RAIMI FANS, ASSEMBLE! For the first time since 2009, the master of gross effects and frenetic cameras is back with an original horror story in Send Help. Rachel McAdams plays a Survivor superfan who gets stuck on an island with her dickhead boss (Dylan O'Brien), and then the antics begin. Think Cast Away meets Misery meets Drag Me to Hell. It's great stuff.

Jason Momoa and Dave Bautista are a pair of cool dudes who, with The Wrecking Crew, set out and did exactly what they intended to do: Make a badass buddy action comedy. The movie finds the pair playing estranged brothers who reunite in Hawaii to investigate their father's mysterious death; From there, we get lots of jokes, and a lot of (very violent!!!) action. It's a good time! Honestly, if they want to make a couple sequels to this, I'd be her for it.

Part This Is Spinal Tap, part Josie and the Pussycats, and part Curb Your Enthusiasm, The Moment is Charli XCX's movie for anyone who enjoys her music, persona, or both. A really fun movie about music, stardom, and celebrity in 2026.

Pillion was technically released initially in 2025 (and was also included on our list of favorite movies of that year), but we didn't want to miss an opportunity to recommend it to people once again. This unique film follows a man (Harry Melling) who engages in an unexpected BDSM relationship with a biker he meets at random (Alexander Skarsgård). The movie is quite the tonal balancing act, at times funny, intense, raunchy, and heartbreaking, but it all comes together by the end. A delightful movie, and a great showcase for both leads.

The classic novel comes to life on the big screen once again, this time from Promising Young Woman and Saltburn director Emerald Fennell, and with Margot Robbie and Jacob Elordi in the lead roles. Fennell, an Academy Award winner for her work on Promising Young Woman, has both big fans and big detractors at this point—but her take her, while book purists haven't been thrilled, is a big, visually stunning epic romance. Robbie and Elordi are both up to the task as well, bringing a charged energy to roles that really need it. Alison Oliver, who recently shined on HBO's Task, is another major highlight in a supporting role. An original soundtrack from Charli XCX helps to set the anachronistic mood and feels like a real cherry on top.

This action-thriller, based on a book by Don Winslow, looks like a very solid entry in the genre that we're going to call "Somewhat Resembles a Michael Mann Film." And reviews have confirmed as much—the movie has often been compared to Heat, and while its tough to compare to Mann's 1995 masterpiece, we'll take just about anything in that vein. Look: If someone tells you there's gonna be a crime thriller in the vein of Heat with Chris Hemsworth, Mark Ruffalo, Halle Berry, and Barry Keoghan leading the cast, how could you not be on board?

One of our coolest directors, Gore Verbinski, makes his grand return with Good Luck, Have Fun, Don't Die—his first movie since 2016's A Cure For Wellness. If you don't know Verbinski by name, you should know several of his movies: the original Pirates of the Caribbean trilogy, The Ring, and Rango are among the standouts. Good Luck follows Sam Rockwell as a man who claims to be from the future and fighting off a rogue artificial intelligence. While the movie takes some pretty tough and labored tangents into on-the-nose satire, Rockwell's performance and the practical effects keep the movie afloat as a fun sci-fi romp.

Despite the title, you don't need to know anything else about Nirvanna the Band the Show the Movie before going to see it. Sure, this story of two inept dudes in a band who just want to play music at a bar—and go through all sorts of ordeals, including time-travel, to do it—has existed before in both web series and television series form. But you can just go in and laugh and the absolute madness of the movie. Trust us—you'll have a good time with this one if you're into "madness that makes you laugh." This is a long-term passion project of Matt Johnson, who became well known recently for directing the underrated BlackBerry. His brash talent is again on display here.

We're always in on Glen Powell, and How to Make a Killing marks his first foray into A24's world as a leading man. This black comedy neo-noir comes from Emily the Criminal director John Patton Ford and follows Powell as a man who decides to take out a few members of his family in order to increase his chance at making a whole bunch of money via inheritance. The supporting cast joining Powell isn't too shabby: Margaret Qualley, Jessica Henwick, Ed Harris, and Topher Grace are all along for the fun.

The Napa Boys is a very specific cut for comedy fans. Remember when all those nondescript American Pie direct-to-video sequels were coming out? "American Pie Presents:.."? The Napa Boys imagines itself as one of those: self-impressed raunchy comedy with little tact—crossed, naturally with the wine bro nature of 2004's Sideways. As a result, we get a movie that presents as a sequel to a franchise that both has long been running out of juice, and, in our world, never was. If you get the truly absurd brand of parody being presented here, you're going to get a real kick out of it.

Hoppers feels like a throwback to the golden age of Pixar. Not only is it an original story (at a time when the legendary animation studio has often been leaning into sequels, prequels, and more), but it's a sweet and funny one at that. Following an animal-lover who uses Avatar-style technology to transfer her consciousness into a robotic beaver body that can discover what animals are thinking and saying, Hoppers actually turns into something of a conspiracy mystery story. With a voice cast that includes Jon Hamm, Dave Franco, and Meryl Streep among others, it's a fun one for the whole family.

Look. This is one of those movies that you really don't have to overthink. It's Alan Ritchson—Reacher himself—taking on a giant alien robot monster thing. This is as much of a throwback to '80s-style action filmmaking as we're ever going to get, and it delivers as promised. The fact that the rest of the cast includes staples like Jai Courtney, Esai Morales, and Dennis Quaid is just a bonus.

Undertone has been positioning itself as A24's next huge horror hit—and we'll see how it lands. The filmfollows a supernatural podcaster who gets sent some particularly spooky recordings; Its soundscape has brought tons of hype, with many calling it the scariest experience of the year. A simple premise like that sometimes makes for a very solid horror movie.

Based on the novel by Andy Weir(who also wrote The Martian), Project Hail Mary is a story of space exploration and a regular guy (played by Ryan Gosling) who gets involved. Phil Lord and Chris Miller (who are responsible for the Spider-Verse movies and directed 21 Jump Street) are behind the camera for this one, which has already proven to be a big, big hit. Gosling is basically on his own out in space for most of this, but it also includes a fun little alien guy named Rocky and a nice supporting performance by Anatomy of a Fall star Sandra Hüller. The visuals here are worth seeing on the biggest screen you can find.

2018's Ready or Not was one of the most fun horror films of the last decade, and now eight years later we get to see Samara Weaving's lead sucked back into the same twisted, bloody, violent games. The supporting cast—including David Cronenberg (!!!), March MH Flex star Elijah Wood, Sarah Michelle Gellar, and The Pitt's Shawn Hatosy—is fantastic. The movie kind of keeps with the form of the first Ready or Not, so if you liked that one, you'll certainly have a fun time with this one.

Forbidden Fruits follows a secret coven of witches operating in a shopping mall. Like, guys, some premises you just have to accept for how good they are and see them out. The movie is a campy, fun, twisty turny ride. Understand what you're getting into—a little bit of horror, a little bit of satire, and some fun twists—and it's going to be a good time.

Zazie Beetz (Atlanta, Deadpool 2) gets to lead her own horror/thriller movie with They Will Kill You, where she plays a woman who answers a help-wanted ad for a housekeeper in a luxury apartment building, only to find herself fighting for her life. The movie is pretty similar in tone to fellow horror/comedy Ready or Not 2, which we just talked about. But They Will Kill You leans more into its John Wick-style action and Kill Bill style plot, which sets it apart. The supporting cast, which includes Patricia Arquette, Heather Graham, and Industry star Myha'la, make it extra worth it.

#4939. Moderate To Severe Hot Flashes Due To Menopause Are Worth Treating. Work With Your Doctor To Develop A Plan

A Bayer-paid spokesperson, OB-GYN, and menopause specialist explains why hot flashes due to menopause happen, how long they can last, and how to prepare for discussions about treatment options with your doctor.

Branded content for Lynkuet® (elinzanetant) 60 mg capsules. Keep reading for Important Safety Information.

For women, menopause is a natural stage of life and is diagnosed when a woman hasn’t had a period for 12 months and can no longer get pregnant. Menopause is not a disease or disorder—it’s a natural part of aging. It’s estimated that over 2 million women in the U.S. enter menopause each year. Almost 50 percent of women in their first year of menopause experience moderate to severe hot flashes.

Diana Bitner, MD, OB-GYN, is a Bayer-paid spokesperson and has been compensated for her time.

But, moderate to severe hot flashes don’t have to be something you simply endure, says Diana Bitner, MD, OB-GYN, a menopause specialist and Bayer-paid spokesperson. There are treatment options available, such as Lynkuet® (elinzanetant), an FDA-approved, hormone-free prescription treatment for the reduction of moderate to severe hot flashes due to menopause.

It’s important to know that women who are pregnant should not take Lynkuet. Lynkuet can cause serious side effects, including central nervous system effects and daytime impairment. Don’t drive or do hazardous activities until these effects go away. Serious side effects also include increased liver blood test values, risk of pregnancy loss, and risk of seizure. The common side effects of Lynkuet include headache, fatigue, dizziness, feeling drowsy or sleepy, stomach (abdominal) pain, rash, diarrhea, and muscle spasms. Please refer to the full Important Safety Information below, and the Full Prescribing Information on Lynkuet.com/pi for more information. Women should speak with an HCP to determine if Lynkuet is right for them.

Here, Dr. Bitner shares what she feels women should know about moderate to severe hot flashes due to menopause—and how to prepare for and discuss treatment options with your doctor.

This interview has been lightly edited for clarity and concision.

Dr. Bitner: A hot flash is a sensation of warmth in the face, neck, and chest, or sudden intense feelings of heat and sweating. They can happen day and night. Hot flashes are one of the most common symptoms of menopause. They are considered mild when they involve a sensation of heat without sweating, moderate when there is a sensation of heat with sweating but you are able to continue activity, and severe when there’s a sensation of heat with sweating that causes you to be unable to continue activity.

Dr. Bitner: I’ve heard some women say that they think their hot flashes are something to just “get through.” I’ve also had many patients who say that their moderate to severe hot flashes can come on unexpectedly and they were surprised that hot flashes can last several years during menopause. Menopause is a phase that all women will go through at some point in their lives, and many women will experience moderate to severe hot flashes due to menopause. On average, moderate to severe hot flashes due to menopause last 3.6 years after diagnosis of menopause, though not all women will experience hot flashes for that period of time or even at all. Individual hot flashes can last anywhere from 1 to 5 minutes, and may occur a few times a week or several times per day or night. Understanding this can help women better understand their hot flashes due to menopause and start a conversation with their healthcare provider.

Dr. Bitner: Women may sometimes feel hesitant to bring up their experience with moderate to severe hot flashes with their healthcare provider. But this is a conversation worth having—particularly when moderate to severe hot flashes are their primary concern.

Something I’ve seen in my practice is that many women come in for a routine visit where there’s a lot to cover. They may not always mention their hot flashes during the visit, but that could be because they are trying to manage hot flashes on their own.

Here’s the thing, though: For women in menopause who have moderate to severe hot flashes, there are treatment options available, like Lynkuet, a prescription treament for moderate to severe hot flashes due to menopause. While some women are aware of treatment options, it isn’t until they speak with a provider that they realize they don’t need to manage moderate to severe hot flashes due to menopause on their own. I want women to know that their hot flashes are worth treating, and I encourage them to talk to their healthcare provider so they can work together on a plan.

Dr. Bitner: It’s helpful to track the frequency and severity of your hot flashes, along with any specific moments hot flashes come on, and if you’re experiencing hot flashes during the day or night. This information may help your doctor determine what treatment options may be right for you.

Dr. Bitner: This is one part of my job that I really appreciate; I believe it’s paramount that women understand what’s happening in their bodies, and I get to serve as a translator of the symptoms occurring and the treatment options available. In the case of moderate to severe hot flashes due to menopause, I often start the conversation by reminding women that they are not alone with this symptom. I then review their treatment options, including Lynkuet, a hormone-free prescription treatment for moderate to severe hot flashes due to menopause. In clinical trials, women experiencing moderate to severe hot flashes who took Lynkuet had fewer and less severe hot flashes, day and night, compared to those who took placebo.* Lynkuet also reduced the number of hot flashes in as early as one week.*

*Based on clinical studies measuring efficacy at 4 and 12 weeks. Individual results may vary.

Dr. Bitner: Women experiencing moderate to severe hot flashes should talk with their healthcare provider about available treatment options, including Lynkuet, to understand what may be right for them.

I also encourage women to speak up throughout the process. When patients feel heard and involved in decisions about their care, they’re more likely to find a treatment option that’s right for them.

Dr. Bitner: My message is that while hot flashes are a common symptom of menopause, you don’t have to navigate them alone. Understand your hot flash frequency and severity and talk with a healthcare provider to explore the treatment options that may be right for you.

LYNKUET is a prescription medicine used to reduce moderate to severe hot flashes (also known as vasomotor symptoms) due to menopause. LYNKUET is not a hormone. Hot flashes are feelings of warmth in the face, neck, and chest, or sudden intense feelings of heat and sweating.

#4938. Solana Drops 'Mainnet Beta' After Six Years: Here's What 1.0 Is All About

Solana Drops 'Mainnet Beta' After Six Years: Here's What 1.0 Is All About

Solana is officially out of beta, more than six years after launching a blockchain that has been handling real money the whole time.

The Solana Foundation on Monday retired the “mainnet beta” label and introduced Solana 1.0, a shared version number for the network's underlying rules. The change is primarily about how developers and validator operators coordinate software updates, not a fresh boost to transaction speed or any other meaningful improvement over what users already have.

Solana launched its mainnet beta on March 16, 2020, and kept the experimental-sounding name even as users traded tokens, built applications, and moved assets across the chain.

Nothing happens to those assets now. “Your SOL, accounts, assets, applications, and transaction history remain the same,” the Foundation said. Users don't need to swap tokens, move wallets or install anything to keep using the network.

Solana has two major validator clients: Agave, developed by Anza, and Firedancer, built independently by Jump Crypto. Each has its own code, release schedule and version numbers, which can make it harder to tell whether different software releases support the same network features.

Solana 1.0 creates a common reference point for the protocol itself. An Agave release and a Firedancer release can support the same protocol version without sharing a software version number.

That distinction matters as the network relies on more than one software implementation. A bug in one client need not affect every validator, although software diversity alone cannot guarantee the network will stay online.

“Announcing a protocol version does not activate every associated improvement at once,” the Foundation warned. Operators still need to check whether their particular software supports a planned upgrade and follow its activation instructions.

The Foundation said it coordinated the change with Anza and the Firedancer team. Its announcement does not describe a new voting system or a change in who governs Solana; the network's governance process for proposals remains separate.

The Foundation credits engineering work that preceded Monday's announcement, particularly Alpenglow and Firedancer. Solana's Alpenglow upgrade went live on October 21, replacing the system validators had used to reach agreement since launch.

Alpenglow targets transaction finality of roughly 150 milliseconds, compared with about 12.8 seconds previously. Finality is the point at which a transaction is considered settled; that improvement came from the October upgrade, not from calling the network 1.0.

Firedancer also reached mainnet in 2025, giving validators a separately developed alternative to Agave. That reduces dependence on a single codebase, though the extent of the protection depends on how widely different clients are actually used.

Solana has reasons to be careful with promises of reliability. Its network went offline for nearly five hours in February 2024, following an outage lasting almost 19 hours a year earlier.

Documentation and block explorers will gradually adopt the new mainnet name, according to the Foundation. Its upgrade tracker still lists Agave 4.4 as planned for November and Agave 4.5 for December, each with its own release and activation requirements.

#4936. Coinbase expands onchain crypto loans to New York via Morpho

Looking for institutional-grade crypto trading? Discover LMAX Digital, the regulated exchange from LMAX Group

Coinbase Borrow is now available in New York, letting residents borrow against their crypto through Morpho on Base.

Crypto exchange operator Coinbase has expanded its onchain crypto loan product to New York residents, completing its rollout across all 50 U.S. states.

The launch follows approval from the New York State Department of Financial Services, a Coinbase spokesperson told The Block.

Asked when Coinbase applied and received approval, Jacob Frantz, head of Coinbase's yield and investment products, said the company had been working with New York regulators since the product launched last year.

"We have been working closely with regulators in New York since launching Coinbase Borrow last year, so that New Yorkers can also access cash without having to sell the crypto assets they believe in," Frantz told The Block. He did not provide application or approval dates or details on the scope of the approval.

With Coinbase Borrow, eligible New York residents can borrow USDC against supported crypto held on Coinbase. The borrowing limits are up to $5 million against bitcoin, $1 million against ether and $100,000 against Solana, subject to eligibility and other applicable limits, the Coinbase spokesperson said.

Customers access Coinbase Borrow through Coinbase, with Morpho providing the onchain lending infrastructure on Base.

The product launched in January 2025 and has since originated more than $3.4 billion in loans. More than $1.7 billion remains outstanding, backed by over $3.2 billion in collateral, Morpho said.

Coinbase has added more collateral options since the launch, most recently tokenized gold via Paxos' Pax Gold (PAXG). It has also introduced fixed-rate loans through Morpho Midnight, allowing borrowers to agree on a rate and maturity before taking out a loan.

Those features are not all available in New York. At launch, customers in the state can borrow against BTC, ETH and SOL, the Coinbase spokesperson said.

Fixed-rate loans and other collateral options, including tokenized gold PAXG, Zcash's ZEC, Hyperliquid's HYPE, XRP and staked assets, are not yet available there, the spokesperson added.

Coinbase also offers a separate USDC lending product through Morpho, where users can earn returns by allocating their USDC across onchain lending markets. That product holds more than $500 million in deposits, according to Morpho, but is also unavailable in New York.

Asked about plans to bring those products to the state, the spokesperson said: "We're excited to continue partnering with regulators to bring better financial services to New Yorkers."

#4934. The 8 Best Winter Coats for Women of 2026, Tested and Reviewed in 10-Degree Weather

Our favorite on this list is from Canada Goose.

Women's Health may earn commission from the links on this page, but we only feature products we believe in. Why Trust Us?

Looking for a winter coat that’ll actually keep you warm this year now that temps are finally starting to drop? We’ve got you covered—literally. At Women’s Health, our editors tested over 20 of this season’s most talked-about winter coats to find the ones that stand up to cold commutes, snowy climates, ski trips, and everything in between

From ultra-warm parkas to sleek puffers, these coats deliver on style, fit, comfort, and serious insulation from top brands like The North Face, lululemon, Columbia, Carhartt, and more. Our absolute favorite? The Canada Goose Shelburne Parka, which stands out for its stylish appearance and ability to keep us warm in extreme temps. To find the best winter coats for women, our style and gear-loving editors tested and evaluated best-selling options based on fit, materials, and warmth level. And, we wore them with tons of different clothes, like leggings with pockets, ski pants, and hoodies.

Looking for more? Check out our other winter clothing guides:

We’ve tested upwards of 20 warm winter coats, but this option from Canada Goose took the winning spot. Why? It’s super stylish, has a versatile fit, and, most importantly, it keeps us super warm in freezing weather.

WH contributor Jennifer Nied spends the colder months in Colorado, and while the NYC cold is definitely bone-chilling, the snow-capped mountains of Colorado are on a whole different level. And, as an avid hiker, Nied really got to put Canada Goose to the test. Her overall consensus: This jacket can withstand super-cold temps without slacking on style.

For a super warm puffer/parka style jacket, this coat is super stylish. The sleek, close-to-body silhouette and mid-thigh length are flattering without sacrificing warmth. We also love the oversized snorkel hood—named for the way it wraps snugly around the face—because it's incredibly cozy and super chic-looking. And, the color options are awesome, too—there’s more than just the black and brown if you’re like us and love a vivid pop of color in the colder months.

We also like this coat because it doesn’t make us feel like the Michelin Man (ha!), but still has ample room for layering underneath. It has a slightly snug fit, and is designed to be worn over light layers or under a bigger coat. But Nied says she could have sized down and still been comfortable, too.

What really sets this parka apart from others is the interior shoulder straps. "This little inside feature lets me easily slip my arms out of the sleeves without removing the whole jacket," she says. "It's handy for turning it into a makeshift backpack when I need to cool off on a crowded subway or in a store." With other coats, she usually ends up awkwardly carrying them in a big bundle whenever she's indoors, she says. There’s also a back vent with snap closures if you get overheated but don’t want to fully take the coat off.

Some additional features: The hood is just the right size—big enough to keep Nied’s head warm without causing a hair disaster. It has multiple closures, like buttons and zippers down the front. Nied is usually a size medium, and says this coat runs true-to-size. The sleeves come with a snug, sweater-like fabric at the end that she can pull over her hands to keep them warm, and the sleeves are also long enough to cover her arms comfortably.

As for warmth, this coat delivers. It’s super warm without even zipping it up—even in near-freezing temps and wind. Nied says it’s definitely the coat she'll wear when the temps plunge to zero for holiday festivities. That’s because the outside is made from a blend of cotton and polyester, which is durable and water-repellent. It’s also made with a 625 fill power made from responsibly sourced down, meaning this jacket keeps you comfortable in temps ranging from fourteen to negative four degrees Fahrenheit. The length, which hits at mid-thigh, also helps keep the chill out.

The only con we have for this jacket is the main pockets. They are lined with fleece that is so cozy for hands, but they have button-up closures instead of zippers, so our things don’t feel as secure.

WH lifestyle director Lindsay Geller is a dog owner, which means she's out early in the morning and late at night to get her pup some exercise. But, since the weather has dropped, she's been on the hunt for a coat she can wear at the chilliest times of the day to keep her warm all walk long. Lucky for her, she got to test this puffer from lululemon, which she says she's "obsessed" with.

This jacket is super sleek and basically covers your entire outfit with its calf-length design, so it's easy to throw it on over any outfit and call it a day. "I wouldn't wear this coat to a formal winter event like a wedding party, but I would pretty much wear it everywhere else like running errands or on a cold vacation," says Geller. "I wish I'd had this coat when I went to Norway last year—it would have been perfect for that."

Geller chose the black color, which she's happy about as it's super easy to style, and goes with pretty much everything.

Because this is one of lululemon's warmest jackets, you would think it would be too hot and bulky to run in, but Geller says that she was surprised at how easily it moved with her body during a morning run with her pup. "I'm used to long puffers feeling super bulky, but this one doesn't," she says, adding that it's still snug and insulated enough to keep her warm. Geller opted for a size medium, and she notes that it fits "just right." She told me that she's worn this coat on freezing cold winter mornings, and it feels like she's wrapped in an "insanely warm, yet still remarkably lightweight blanket" the entire time. "Safe to say, I'll be living in this coat until spring (at least)," she says.

Her main con is the zipper can be tricky to maneuver at the bottom, but once you hear it click, it works. However, she says it can get frustrating just trying to get the bottom part of the zipper to work.

"I absolutely adore my Columbia down jacket," says WH news and features editor Currie Engel. It's her go-to jacket for all her winter occasions.

"Lately, I've been rocking it everywhere—from the gym to dates and even at work," she says. That’s because it strikes a perfect style balance, with no over-the-top designs that lean too casual or too fancy—except maybe the fur-lined hood (which is removable!). And with a relaxed silhouette, it flatters the body without looking too bulky—despite the slightly longer mid-thigh length. This makes it a match for anything in her wardrobe.Engel opted for a size medium, and she notes that it fits perfectly. "I love the length because it’s not so long that it feels like a dress, but it's long enough to keep my whole body warm," she notes.Engel is a huge fan of how big the pockets are. "I was able to fit my wallet, phone, keys, and more in there with absolute ease (and no bulges!)." She adds that the outer fabric, which is made of polyester, is *super* luxurious and thick without the hefty price tag. The insulated interior is made of the brand's patented Omni-Heat Reflective lining, which reflects and retains body heat without adding bulk. Plus, the outer is made with 100 percent polyester, which is a welcome bonus because its small synthetic fibers help keep you super warm, and is water-resistant to help wick away sweat or light rain. It’s also insulated with 100% synthetic down—making it a more affordable option that still keeps you warm in cold, rainy weather.While there weren't many cons, Engel told me she wishes the hood could zip off.

This puffer goes all the way down past the knee to keep you nice and protected (and extra warm!). TBH, it’s hard to find a long puffer that’s actually flattering. Most look like they’re swallowing you up—but this one is a welcome exception. “It’s surprisingly lightweight, so it doesn’t look super big and bulky when you put it on,” says Lauture.

But don’t get it twisted: Although it’s light, it’s still incredibly warm thanks to a 700-plus fill power goose down insulation made to keep you comfortable in temperatures up to negative 48 degrees Fahrenheit! Plus, the 100% recycled polyester shell and lining are water-repellent and wind-resistant, making this coat a great option for a variety of climates.

Lauture also loves how versatile this coat is. And, it has many bells and whistles that make it even more worth it, like a detachable hood, thumb holes, fleece-lined pockets, and snap closures down both the front and sides of the coat. It also nails that minimalist, high-end look with its clean seams, matte finish, and perfectly relaxed fit. This jacket looks just as great with a pair of slim-fit jeans and loafers as it does with ski pants and boots.

One thing we ran into a lot with long coats is that they were too long for more petite people, but we found that this one hits at the calf no matter what height you are, short or tall. We do find that, in terms of puffers, we like the soft, airy texture of the Super Puff better than this option, as it’s a bit on the heavier side.

While the SuperPuff is on the pricier side, it’s well worth the investment for its durability and performance in harsh weather, says Saladino. “It’s not just a winter coat—it’s a statement piece that’s both functional and fashionable,” she says. Case in point: It comes in a variety of colors and lengths depending on your preference. Even the shorter hip-length version Saladino tested came in clutch for staying warm while on the go.

It stands out as one of the most stylish winter coats with its luxe, oversized fit and wide stitched panels that give it an edgy look. We also love the matte, nylon outer material and monochrome buttons that look super clean. It’s effortlessly chic and doesn’t skimp on function.

Warmth will not be questioned in this puffer. Saladino wore this during a brutally cold NYC afternoon and found that it kept her incredibly cozy. How? It’s filled with 700-plus fill-power premium down that provides some major insulation. The nylon outer is also water-repellent and wind-resistant, so you don’t have to panic if you get stuck in harsh conditions.

We appreciate that this coat has zippered pockets, so our belongings never fall out. Another bonus feature: It comes with a detachable hood. And we were pleasantly surprised that this coat runs true-to-size. We opted for our normal size and found that there was still room to fit a hoodie underneath.

This jacket is extremely warm with its fleece interior and 100% synthetic insulation, but it’s also one of the most durable options on this list. Its silicone-coated nylon exterior is water-repellent, so it keeps you dry if you get stuck in the rain or snow. Plus, it’s made with a wind-fighting nylon tech for extreme weather conditions, making it great for winter hikers. Although it has all these features, we found that the coat actually still feels lightweight. A bonus point is that it’s shorter than many other coats on this list, so it’s not as bulky and doesn't feel restrictive.

This coat gives total gorpcore vibes with its boxy fit and utilitarian details (like the patch logo and zip chest pocket) that feel effortlessly cool. The matte fabric and subtle branding add to the street-style edge that we find pairs well with everything from jeans to tailored trousers.

We also love that it comes with a hood, but it’s not removable, which marked it down a few points in our book. That being said, this coat is great for harsher conditions. Another pro? This coat comes equipped with plenty of pockets, including interior ones. So, when you’re out and about, you don’t have to worry about where you’re going to store your belongings.

In terms of size, we def recommend sizing down because this coat can look super bulky if it’s too big. However, we found that sizing down eliminated some of the thickness in the coat.

Many jackets on this list are water-resistant, but this option from Rains is fully waterproof. It kept our tester dry in light rain, thanks to the water-repellent finish. On top of that, we found this jacket to be breathable, lightweight, and super-durable. Even in the harsh NYC winds, we found that it protected us from the elements and kept us warm and dry.

Style contributor Rose Lauture recently went on a trip to Vermont and tested this coat while she was out there. “As soon as I walked out from the airport and felt the chilly air hit my face, I knew I made the right decision wearing this coat,” she says. The coat is equipped with 100% synthetic insulation and waterproof fabric which helped keep her super-warm and dry. “I spent a good amount of time outdoors in Vermont as we went hiking and played pickleball, and the coat held up well,” Lauture says.

As far as extra additions go, we love that this puffer has fleece pockets for extra warmth and a large, insulated drawstring hood for another layer of protection. Plus, the coat zips up past the neck all the way to the mouth to seal in heat.

It’s also super stylish. It’s not too puffy that it adds unnecessary width, but it still has that streetwear-esque puffer style. The rubberized, monochromatic (and weatherproof!) hardware also upgrades the look of the coat. Plus, it looks effortlessly cool when you only zip it halfway—the two-way zipper lets the coat fall open just enough to reveal the glossy interior lining, adding a cool contrast that feels very street style-ready.

We also appreciate that it comes in a variety of matte and shiny colors, so there are plenty of options to choose from. And, it’s super easy to take care of, too. “I was hesitant at first with the light color of the coat and how it might get dirty quickly, but the fabric is so easy to clean,” says Lauture, who used a cloth to wipe down the coat of any marks. However, you can easily throw it in the washer with cold water to clean it.

As far as fit goes, it is a bit oversized, but since it’s supposed to have more of that streetstyle look, we like its slightly larger fit. Want it to be a bit more snug? Opt for one size down.

In our opinion, a puffer jacket is a must-have for every wardrobe because it keeps you warm and pairs great with any outfit. But through our testing, we’ve learned that not all puffers are created equally—until we discovered this one from The North Face.

Despite its shorter length, it’s one of the best options on our list for braving the cold, thanks to ultra-warm 700-fill down insulation and an insulated hood that seamlessly packs into the collar. It’s also made with a durable nylon outer and lining, making this a great water-resistant and moisture-wicking option, too.

“This jacket is one of the warmest offerings from The North Face, and it’s also windproof, making it perfect for braving those chilly winter days,” says Saladino. Her fave feature? The tuckable hood. She loves how easy it is to fold into the collar when it’s not in use.

We also love the retro vibe of this winter jacket. It has a boxy, relaxed fit that’s super chic and flattering. According to Saladino, it has a timeless look that feels both classic and fresh. “The zip pockets on the outside are super practical, and the interior pocket means I can leave my handbag behind during the colder months,” says Saladino. “Overall, it’s a stylish, functional, and incredibly cozy choice for cold weather.” The entire jacket also easily stows into the right-hand pocket, so it’s super easy to pack.

Our one recommendation? Size up for a roomier fit. We found that going true-to-size left us feeling a bit too snug and unable to layer heavier clothing underneath. REI doesn't currently carry this red shade, but it has a cute berry colorway and neutral options to choose from.

Before buying a winter coat, think about where you’ll be using it. Are you living in a big city or a rural area? Does it get crazy cold or more temperate in the winter? How active are you? Once you've decided what you need, you can get into the nitty-gritty of coat shopping.

The key to a warm winter coat? Insulation. But there are two main types to consider: down and synthetic. Learning a bit about them can guide you in choosing the right coat for your lifestyle.

The bottom line: If you live in a wet environment and want to spend less money, go with synthetic insulation. If you live in a drier, colder place and are willing to splurge a bit more, opt for a coat that has down insulation.

You want to make sure your winter jacket is warm enough to last through many seasons. And, in order to do that, you want to make sure the materials your jacket is made of are super weather-resistant, especially if you’re in an area with harsh conditions and need extra warmth and protection. #4933. The 60 Best New Shows of 2026 (and 1 More We Can't Wait For)

We've got murder mysteries, stories of love and lust, and lots and lots of Yellowstone. And that's just the beginning.

THE IDEA OF "new" television shows is a little bit of a tricky one these days. Sure, we do still get a fair share of truly new, exciting, unique ideas each year—just look at shows like Severance a couple years ago and Pluribus last year. Shows like last year's The Lowdown—rich, well-written, character-focused stories—still draw major stars like Ethan Hawke and still hit in a big way for audiences that watch it. If someone was being dramatic and wanted to say original TV was dead, dying, or on life support, there's plenty of evidence out there to throw in their face.

But at the same time, they aren't entirely wrong. For one reason or another, so much of the TV landscape—even shows we're really excited for—are based around something that in one way or another already exists.

Look, we can't beat too much around the bush: People love nostalgia, people love things they recognize and remember, and it can be pretty hard to get anyone to even attempt to give their attention to something new, let alone get really into it in the way we all like to with the very best of TV. Which is why we kind of have two different options here—people need to be really trusting of word of mouth and really aware when something is a really good new, original show (because no one likes to waste their time with a piece of junk), and we just need to really hope that all the remakes, reboots, reimaginings, and re-whatevers are good.

And they should be! HBO's Lanterns is modeled after True Detective, stars Kyle Chandler and Aaron Pierre as the titular Green Lanterns, and counts Watchmen genius Damon Lindelof as a producer. Of course it’s good. Below, we're going to keep track all year. We're charting the shows we already know are good. We're charting the shows we think might be good. And we're charting the shows that may not even come out this year, but if they do... they still might not be good. But, again, say it with us: We're choosing to be hopeful.

Netflix has been really good of late at the pulpy, potboiler, limited series, and His & Hers is the latest in that winning streak. The show follows a detective (Jon Bernthal) and his estranged journalist wife (Tessa Thompson) as they both hunt for answers when a local woman—whom they both have a close connection to—winds up dead. Based on Alice Feeney's book of the same name, His & Hers is exactly how this kind of show should be: Juicy, fun, easy to watch, and filled with really good actors.

In shrinking its story down to a more intimate one that takes place between the margins of major universe events, Game of Thrones takes a page out of the Andor handbook with A Knight of the Seven Kingdoms (based on George R.R. Martin's Dunk and Egg novellas). This short series, which follows a big, humble, anxious hedge knight (former professional rugby playerPeter Claffey)and his little friend/squire (Dexter Sol Ansell) is a true breath of fresh air for Thrones fans on both a story and character level. It's a delight.

Doesn't the premise of Ponies just sound fun? This spy series set in '70s Moscow follows a pair of women working with the CIA who find themselves at the midst of a vast conspiracy when their husbands both die under mysterious circumstances. And those women are played by The White Lotus's Haley Lu Richardson and Game of Thrones queen Emilia Clarke. Sometimes something that sounds like a winner just turns out to be one.

The Fall and Rise of Reggie Dinkins (NBC/Peacock)

This show about a disgraced former football player (Tracy Morgan) and a documentary filmmaker following him (Daniel Radcliffe) comes from the team behind 30 Rock, so you know you're going to get several jokes per minute. Plus, Morgan and Radcliffe are no slouches themselves. The show had a special debut in January and will continue on a regular schedule later in February.

At the very least, Wonder Man is among the best shows Marvel ever made—and you could make a case that it's at the top of the list. Yahya Abdul Mateen II plays the titular hero (aka actor Simon Williams) as the kind of guy we love to love in this sort of story: humble, well-meaning, charismatic, and ambitious. But when he meets fellow actor (and former fake terrorist) Trevor Slattery (Ben Kingsley) and learns that his favorite movie from childhood is being remade by an acclaimed director, everything changes. Wonder Man isn't just a good Marvel show, but a good show about people, movies, and friendship period. Let's hope the MCU takes notes from what worked so well here and keeps the streak going in the future.

One of America's great cultural institutions made its grand return in 2026: The Muppet Show! This version—coming from executive producers Seth Rogen and Evan Goldberg—is directly modeled on the original Muppet Show, which means special guests, musical performances, comedy sketches, and lots of fun. The first episode, which featured special guest star Sabrina Carpenter, was an absolute delight for anyone who likes Kermit, Miss Piggy, and friends (or who just likes laughing and having a good time). For now, it's just this one episode, but if the reaction is strong enough (and it seems like it might be), the show will come back in full.

The latest entry in producer Ryan Murphy's American Story universe is called Love Story, and follows the romance and life between Carolyn Bessette Kennedy and John F. Kennedy Jr. The show is, however, much better than that tabloid-y description sounds; Sarah Pidgeon, who plays Carolyn, is a star, coming off her Tony-nominated role in the Fleetwood Mac-inspired play Stereophonic. But Paul Anthony Kelly, who plays JFK Jr., is a real discovery—it's his first role (he was previously a model), and he truly feels like a reincarnation of the late attorney/magazine publisher/dashing public figure. Of course, this is a story that ends in an extreme tragedy—so if you get invested, be sure to have your tissues ready.

This wild documentary series looks at different disputes between neighbors, telling compelling and often escalating true stories that will truly floor you in the depiction of their very-real truth. Think about this less as a story about the legalities of these disputes, and more a look into some larger-than-life characters through an often trippy, absurd lens. The series is produced by Josh Safdie and Ronald Bronstein, coming off of their recent success on the Oscar-nominated Marty Supreme.

The new season of Scrubs brings back almost all of the original cast, including Zach Braff, Donald Faison, and Sarah Chalke. And audiences who love and/or remember that trio and most of the show's original dramedy premise should be pleased with this new version of the beloved aughts sitcom. The last season aired in 2010, so we're OK with calling this 16-years-later revival a 'new' show.

DTF St. Louis follows trio of languishing adults—played by the electric trio of Jason Bateman, Linda Cardellini, and David Harbour—who get involved in a love triangle and general madness that results in one of them winding up dead. You may think you have an idea of what you're getting into with this show based on the cast and that premise, but believe us—all of your expectations will be upended. DTF St. Louis is a tonal balancing act, a show that bounces between hilarious dark comedy, compelling mystery, and gutting, relatable drama. It's one of the best shows of the year.

The second age of Yellowstone begins in earnest with Marshals, a 13-episode drama that airs on CBS (and streams on Parmaount+ either simultaneously or a day later, depending on which tier of subscription you have). The series focuses on Luke Grimes's character Kayce, and how an old SEAL Team leader (Logan Marshall-Green) recruits him into his Marshal squad. There's at least one more Yellowstone spinoff coming in 2026—Dutton Ranch—and so this is the one leading the charge.

One of the busiest men in show business these days—on both the big and small screen—is Guy Ritchie, and his newest endeavor takes him back to a world he's inhabited a couple times before. Young Sherlock follows, well, a Young Sherlock Holmes. And as you can imagine, it follows Arthur Conan Doyle's famous detective as he solves a mystery. Hero Fiennes Tiffin plays the titular character, and Colin Firth is also part of the show's cast. If you're into that, you'll have a fun time! It's an enjoyable show.

The erotic thriller is back! Or, well, juicy erotic character study dramedy? Whatever we want to call it, Netflix's Vladimir is one of the year's most exciting new shows. Based on the novel of the same name, this show follows a longtime literature professor at a college (Rachel Weisz, constantly breaking the fourth wall) who finds herself in the midst of controversy when her fellow professor husband (John Slattery) gets caught sleeping with students. She takes this as an opportunity to switch things up a bit, and so she becomes smitten with her very sexy new colleague (Leo Woodall). It's a fun, zippy, juicy time—and kind of like if Deadpool was actually about a smart woman in academia who's spinning her wheels and maybe just a little bit horny.

From the mold of Ted Lasso and Shrinking comes Rooster, which stars Steve Carell and counts Lasso and Shrinking co-creator Bill Lawrence (who also made Scrubs and Cougar Town) as its showrunner. Carell plays an author who heads to help his professor daughter on a college campus... and becomes enamored with life there. Imagine Back to School but with some middle-age soul-searching and academia at play? Sure! HBO's got another winner on their hands with this one—and maybe Carell can get the Emmy that he somehow never got for The Office.

There are 29 books in the Scarpetta series, and, now, one TV show on Prime Video starring Nicole Kidman and Jamie Lee Curtis. The series follows forensic pathologist Dr. Kay Scarpetta (Kidman) as she solves a crime—but the show is so much more than just that. In a way, Scarpetta is destined to fit into Prime Video's roster of rock-solid procedural murder mysteries, which also includes Reacher, Cross, Bosch, and plenty more. But it's got a little bit of an extra chaotic oomph—helped out by the star-studded cast that also includes Bobby Cannavale and Simon Baker—that make it worth your while and a unique, fun show.

Sunny Nights, which aired in Australia last year, now makes its U.S. debut on Hulu. The premise is simple: A pair of siblings (played by the very funny Will Forte and D'Arcy Carden) want to start a spray tan business, but wind up entrenched in the criminal underworld. Whoops! Forte and Carden have been two of our finest comedic actors for a while—with ability to play depth in addition to that humor—and the show thrives when they're at their strongest. A solid watch for anyone looking for something light but compelling.

This series—from Yellowstone super writer/producer Taylor Sheridan—follows Stacy Clyburn (Michelle Pfeiffer) and her family, as they move from the busy, stressful world of New York City to a more rustic setting out in beautiful Montana after a totally unforseen tragedy. Kurt Russellplays her husband, Preston, with his usual endless charisma, while the supporting cast includes the likes of Matthew Fox and Suits star Patrick J. Adams. Sheridan does his usual zigging and zagging in The Madison—the tone can sometimes shift from very sad to zany and comedic, and, as usual, there's a bit of social commentary speechifying buried in almost every scene. But if you're on board with the writing style he uses in shows like Yellowstone and Landman, you'll probably be OK with it here, especially if you're ready for a heavier and more contemplative tone. This show was originally planned to be part of the Yellowstone connected universe, but those plans have since been changed; It's now a new story, but with that Montana setting, you still get to look at all sorts of beautiful landscapes.

After striking gold a couple years ago with Jury Duty, Prime Video gives its grand Truman Show-esque experiment another try with a second season called Company Retreat. This time around, we follow a regular guy who thinks he’s working as a temp for a hot sauce company and joining them on their annual company bonding retreat. Of course, everyone around him is actually an actor in a scripted, engineered situation. It’s a little goofier than the first season, but seeing how everything plays out is compelling, often very funny television nonetheless. A worthy follow-up, and, honestly, we might just watch these as long as they feel like making them.

Riz Ahmed is the creator and star of Bait, a show about an actor who thinks he's about to get offered the role of a lifetime—James Bond!—and the madness that spirals out of such a revelation. If you're a fan of Ahmed's (and why wouldn't you be?) this will be a fun ride.

Something Very Bad Is Going To Happen (Netflix)

Camila Morrone (Daisy Jones and the Six) and Adam DiMarco(The White Lotus) are set to get married in this horror series from showrunner Haley Z. Boston (who worked on the very underrated Brand New Cherry Flavor) and producers The Duffer Brothers. And not to oversell, but Something Very Bad Is Going to Happen is the best horror show I've seen in quite some time. While the show plays with familiar settings and tropes—you may think of Ready or Not or Midsommar during the show's eight episodes—it's so filled with Ari Aster-esque dread and stunning, striking camera work that it doesn't even matter. Horror fans are in for an absolute treat with this one.

#4931. Jito’s Lucas Bruder says crypto builders need to ‘slow down’ and fix security weaknesses

Looking for institutional-grade crypto trading? Discover LMAX Digital, the regulated exchange from LMAX Group

Jito is expanding its security team and using AI for defense as Bruder calls the next two years critical for crypto builders.

Jito Labs co-founder and CEO Lucas Bruder says crypto developers need to pump the brakes on building to focus on security as attackers use AI tools to find weaknesses in their defenses.

Speaking to The Block on Tuesday at the Solana Breakpoint conference in London, Bruder said the next two years are going to be pivotal for teams to fix unresolved issues in their software, which he referred to as "technical debt."

"I’m a fan of moving fast, but now I think the next two years are gonna be super critical to slow down a little bit, fix your tech debt, go back and solve it," he said.

Bruder noted that Jito has been working on bolstering its security operation for the past year and a half. The company hired a security lead from Galaxy, added another security employee six months ago, and is now looking to hire two more.

"It's very intense out there," he said. "We've seen that the people that are doing this are very patient and very motivated. And so you just have to be very careful at a lot of layers of security."

For crypto companies in particular, this could mean improving how they manage multi-sig wallets, deploy software, and tighten hiring procedures.

"It's really a process that you need in your company," Bruder said. "So it’s not an afterthought, it’s like you have to bake it into the way that you work."

AI is also now being put to use on both sides of the security war. Asked about using AI to review code for vulnerabilities, Bruder said Jito has been doing similar work internally.

"On one hand, like they are using LLMs to attack you and on the other side, you can use the same LLM to help defend yourself," he said.

"You really just have to be proactive," Bruder added. "Don’t wait, just get ahead of it."

#4930. 'Tokenization Is Not the Finish Line': Jupiter to Let Users Borrow Against Bullish Shares

'Tokenization Is Not the Finish Line': Jupiter to Let Users Borrow Against Bullish Shares

Jupiter, the largest trading platform on Solana, is bringing Bullish's shares onchain as collateral, as part of a push to put tokenized assets to work.

The company will launch a dedicated, permissioned market on its lending platform, Jupiter Lend, starting with Bullish's NYSE-listed BLSH stock, Jupiter tweeted on Monday. More issuer tokens will follow, though the market won't be available in all jurisdictions, it added.

A NYSE-listed company is bringing its own shares directly to Jupiter Lend.

Today at Breakpoint, we announced our partnership with @Bullish to launch a dedicated, permissioned $BLSH market.

For the first time, Issuer Tokens can be used as collateral inside Solana’s… pic.twitter.com/rWWqwOcWmK

— Jupiter (@JupiterExchange) November 16, 2026

Unlike many tokenized stocks, which give holders a claim on a share, Bullish's issuer-sponsored token "is itself the share," Jupiter COO Kash Dhanda said in a presentation at Solana's Breakpoint conference in London.

Users will be able to borrow against them with fully onchain liquidations in an "institutional-grade lending market," and integrations with qualified custodians, he said. Bullish acquired Equiniti, one of the world's largest transfer agents, earlier this year, Dhanda noted.

Dhanda framed the announcements around what he called the "post-tokenization era." Most tokenized assets today are "parked, not productive," he said.

Of the roughly $460 billion in tokenized assets tracked by data platform RWA.xyz, only about $39.5 billion is actually onchain and can be moved off the issuer's platform, and just $3.4 billion is used in DeFi, according to DeFiLlama, Dhanda said, a "utilization gap" of 99%.

"There is this myth, and this is the thing that's misunderstood: 'If you put it on chain, they will come'," he said. "This is not the field of dreams," he added, arguing that, "Tokenization is not the finish line. It is actually the starting line."

Jupiter launched two other products alongside the Bullish market. The Jupiter Global Passport lets users verify their identity to buy permissioned assets, while keeping their information as private as possible using zero-knowledge data sharing, Dhanda said. It is live with KYC verification, with onchain credit scores and proof of wealth to follow, and the company is exploring licenses in different jurisdictions.

Jupiter Liquidity Services, meanwhile, will help asset issuers design their markets, seed initial capital, find market makers and integrate with Jupiter's routing so that their tokens are available across the platforms that use it. "You integrate once, you will be available everywhere," Dhanda said.

"Shallow credit markets don't drive liquidity on chain," he added. "If you cannot do more with your onchain asset than you can do with the off-chain version of it, you're probably not going to switch."

Jupiter says it has handled more than $500 billion in trading volume so far this year and paid out $162 million in yield. The Breakpoint announcements follow the company's launch last week of token baskets, yield vaults and a rebuilt portfolio, and come as other venues bring tokenized stocks to Solana. #4928. Want to Turn Back the Clock? These 10 Diets May Help You Age Better

You’ve got way more options than just the Mediterranean diet.

When healthy aging is the goal, it makes sense to try everything you can to make it happen. That means doing your best to exercise regularly, keep up with doctor's appointments, and eat a well-balanced diet. You have lots of options when it comes to the last one—but it can be hard to know which of the many popular eating plans is right for you. Thankfully, new research has helped narrow the choices.

The study, which was published in Nature Communications, analyzed several different diets to see how they impacted biological aging. (Biological aging is the age of your cells, while your chronological age is how old you are.) Popular eating plans like the Mediterranean diet and the DASH (Dietary Approaches to Stop Hypertension) diet made the cut, of course, but several lesser-known diets did too. Here’s what to know.

Meet the experts: Jessica Cording, RD, author of The Little Book of Game-Changers; Keri Gans, RD, author of The Small Change Diet; and Sonya Angelone, RD, PhD, a former spokeswoman for the Academy of Nutrition and Dietetics and a San Francisco-based dietitian.

For the study, researchers analyzed data from 6,470 participants who were 30 and older. Researchers looked at some of the participants' biomarkers that correlated with biological age and compared that with information about their diets.

After analyzing the data, researchers found that healthier eating in general was linked with slower biological aging, no matter which diet people chose. Each specific eating plan offered an edge with certain perks, though. Case in point: The DASH diet (which is specifically meant to stop hypertension) had more cardiovascular benefits for biological aging, while the MIND diet (which combines the Mediterranean and DASH diets for brain health) offered cognitive perks. But researchers discovered that there were a lot of shared biological aging benefits between the different types of diets.

These are the 10 diets flagged as being good for biological aging:

All of these diets are slightly different, but there are a few common threads. "They generally emphasize fruits, vegetables, whole grains, and other nutrient-dense foods," says Keri Gans, RD, author of The Small Change Diet.

The diets also stress the importance of minimally processed foods, while limiting refined carbs, added sugars, and processed meats, according to Sonya Angelone, RD, PhD, a former spokeswoman for the Academy of Nutrition and Dietetics and a San Francisco-based dietitian. "The recommended foods provide fiber, antioxidants, polyphenols, vitamins, minerals, and healthy fats that support metabolic health and help protect cells from oxidative stress and chronic inflammation," she says. Oxidative stress and chronic inflammation are both linked to a higher risk of disease, Angelone points out.

These diets also support the heart, brain, and digestive systems, says Jessica Cording, RD, author of The Little Book of Game-Changers. "All of these things factor into the aging process and somebody's quality of life as they age," she says. "When you're eating to support these different organ systems, you support your longevity and lower your risk of disease."

There are a few things to take away from the findings, according to dietitians. One is that there isn't a single eating plan that's superior to others when it comes to longevity. "It's the overall quality of what we eat consistently that matters most, rather than following a particular diet or avoiding individual foods," Gans says.

While there are plenty of diet plans out there that claim they can help you live longer, Angelone stresses this: "Healthy aging doesn’t have to include expensive foods, supplements, or restrictive diets."

Finally, the study underscores the power of nutrition in keeping you healthy. "Our genes are not our destiny," Angelone says. "We can change the expression of our genes—genomics—with nutrition and lifestyle habits."

Supporting healthy aging with the way you eat means giving your body the fuel it requires to function well, Angelone says. "Healthy aging isn’t about finding a perfect diet or miracle food or supplement," she says. "It is about consistently providing foods that supply nutrients needed by our bodies to function optimally, repair cellular damage, and protect themselves. This will impact how we age."
